newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: NDB says share sale not to impact bank.
newsitem.headline: NDB says share sale not to impact bank.

text.p: The sale of majority of the shares of Sri Lanka's National Development Bank (NDB) to foreign investors will not affect the bank's policies or management, senior officials said on Tuesday.
NDB last week sold 16.5 million of its shares to foreign funds after an early conversion of debentures.

Although foreign investors will now own most of NDB shares, it will continue to operate according to the parliamentary act under which it was set up with the present management retaining control, Ranjith Fernando, NDB's chief executive officer told a news conference on Tuesday.

There had been criticism on the transfer of the majority shareholding to foreign investors, but the government would not have realised the 4.3 billion rupees on the sale of the 16.5 million shares had they been offered in Sri Lanka, Fernando said.
"The local market cannot absorb a share offer of this size so the major portion had to be sought from the international market," he said.

The share offer was taken up by foreign fund managers who were attracted by the bank's performance and return on investment and had no interest in joining the bank's board of directors, Fernando added.
The NDB will continue to lend only to local entrepreneurs, Chairman Nimal Sanderatne said.
"Changes at NDB will not be to do with privatization but with the concepts of universal banking and economic conditions," he said.
